On-screen prompt / action: New chest pain reported. STOP exercise/EVA preparation, stabilize/secure the crewmember, and summon the crew medical officer now. Start event log.
Engineer / clinical note: Do not wait for sensor confirmation; this is a training/demo protocol.

On-screen prompt / action: Is the crewmember responsive to voice or touch?
Any red flags: crushing/pressure-type pain, pain radiating to arm/jaw/back, shortness of breath, cold sweat, fainting, severe weakness, or worsening/persistent discomfort?
Engineer / clinical note: No red flags does not exclude serious causes.

On-screen prompt / action: HIGH PRIORITY: Continue immediate onboard medical assessment. Notify flight surgeon NOW through the earliest channel; do not delay onboard care for Earth response. Follow approved crew medical kit/ECG/atmosphere procedures and suspend EVA.
Urgency: Flight surgeon now + crew medical response
Engineer / clinical note: No drugs, doses, oxygen, IV or device-specific therapy prescribed by app.

On-screen prompt / action: New unexplained chest pain still requires crew medical evaluation now. Keep the crewmember resting and supported; pause critical duties. Assess vitals only with available validated instruments.
Engineer / clinical note: Do not auto-clear because the pulse/SpO2 appears normal.

On-screen prompt / action: Is pain ongoing, recurring, or worsening, OR have new red-flag symptoms appeared?
Engineer / clinical note: Crew retains responsibility for clinical evaluation.

On-screen prompt / action: Pain has eased, but the case is NOT automatically cleared. Document timing and symptoms, continue crew medical evaluation and request flight-surgeon review as appropriate. EVA/critical-task return requires authorized clearance.
Urgency: Crew assessment; further escalation per medical officer
Engineer / clinical note: A resolved episode can still be clinically serious.
